reason: Conversation 1 reached the likely cause efficiently: it asked corded/cordless and smells up front, had the customer rule out the socket and inspect the cable, and once the taped section and flicker were disclosed it told her to stop using it, not wiggle the cable, and route the repair to her son or a vacuum shop with sensible options (shorten and re-plug, or full cable replacement) and realistic costs. Conversation 2 fixated on a thermal cut-out for two turns despite the cable tape being volunteered, never had the socket tested, pushed a torch/blockage check she couldn't do, and inserted an irrelevant model-number panel; it only arrived at the broken-cable conclusion because the customer herself raised the flicker. Conversation 1 was somewhat overconfident ('That's your answer') without noting the fuse or switch remain unexcluded, but its safety advice and escalation were sound and far more useful than Conversation 2's late, bare 'get a qualified person' with no practical path.
